audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim at Brown 1986: xiv in the held PDF, and independently corroborated in the held Brown 1973 (PL C-26) at p. 307 (rule stated for Toaripi with examples) and p. 350 ('In stress, juncture, and intonation Orokolo is in agreement with Toaripi'). (2) The deciding source is a dictionary introduction, but by the sole authority on the family, and it agrees with his 1973 sketch; Glottolog's actual bibliography (fetched sources) lists no phonology article, instrumental study, or other grammar besides Brown's own 1972 thesis. The classification fixed penultimate primary stress with a secondary two syllables to its left is exactly what both held sources say; the only soft spots are (a) 'normally' plus a closed class of final-stressed nominative pronouns (and Toaripi fáitora), which does not threaten a fixed-penult coding, and (b) iteration of secondary stress beyond one 'minor stres
